name: Cobalt working session
notes: Working session with Elena and Tom at Cobalt Bank on Treasury add-on scoping: cash-position fields, who owns the weekly Treasury forecast, and how it sits next to the banking CRM. Renewal was mentioned only as something already in a separate negotiation, not the topic of this meeting.

action_items.text: Send a scoping note for the Treasury add-on: objects, permissions, and a proposed sandbox
Confirm which Treasury fields can leave the core banking system

transcript.speaker: Elena Park
transcript.text: Priya, Sam — thanks. We booked this as a Cobalt working session specifically for Treasury add-on scoping. I don't want to spend it on the renewal. That one's already in negotiation with our procurement folks and a different thread.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: We'll stay on Treasury. Tom, you're closer to the product side, right?

transcript.speaker: Tom Wu
transcript.text: Yes. I own Treasury ops. The add-on we kicked off is about cash-position forecasting for corporate clients, not about renewing the core Helios seats. Different budget, different owner. If we mix them, Finance will reject both.

transcript.speaker: Sam Ortiz
transcript.text: Makes sense. For scoping I need: which object is the cash position, who is allowed to edit a Treasury commit, and whether those users even have Helios logins today. Renewal users are AEs. Treasury users are probably not.

transcript.speaker: Elena Park
transcript.text: Correct. AEs should not see client cash. The Treasury add-on needs a tighter permission set. I'm fine if the renewal keeps going on its own timeline. Please don't shove Treasury fields into that negotiation as a sweetener. It muddies the paper.

transcript.speaker: Tom Wu
transcript.text: Functionally we need a weekly Treasury meeting that looks like a forecast meeting but the rows are cash positions, not opportunities. If Helios can only model opportunities, we have to say so now rather than pretend during a demo.

transcript.speaker: Sam Ortiz
transcript.text: We can model a Treasury object with a commit and a manager overlay. It is not the opportunity object. That's why this is an add-on, not a configuration of what you already bought. I'll put that in the scoping note so nobody 'just uses deals' as a shortcut.

transcript.speaker: Elena Park
transcript.text: Good. Amount on our side for the add-on is still the discovery number we shared — forty-five-ish. I'm not asking you to re-price the renewal in this room. I'm asking whether scoping is done enough to put a sandbox in front of two Treasury PMs next week.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: That's the bar. Sam will send the object list and permission matrix. Tom, if you can confirm which fields are allowed out of the core banking system, we won't design a sandbox we can't populate.

transcript.speaker: Tom Wu
transcript.text: I'll confirm. Constraint: no raw account numbers in Helios. Masked client names are fine. If your sandbox needs a join key, we can use our internal Treasury id.

transcript.speaker: Elena Park
transcript.text: Last thing. Legal already has the renewal redlines. If you send a new MSA for Treasury, send it as an addendum, not a replacement. I don't want the renewal lawyers to think we reopened their deal.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Addendum. We'll keep the threads separate in email too — Treasury add-on in the subject, not 'Cobalt renewal plus.' Thanks for keeping us honest.

transcript.speaker: Tom Wu
transcript.text: Appreciate it. Talk after the scoping note.

transcript.speaker: Sam Ortiz
transcript.text: I'll have it to you this afternoon.
